utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Yes, please continue Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would like to start with a correction to one of my calculations. Yesterday at page 38584, I asserted that the pie slice which appears at page 161 of the B/C/S version of your report, which is D3551 has an area of 4.5 million square metres. The correct figure is, in fact, 5.45 million square metres. Now, I don't believe that should have any impact on the answer that you provided, but if you do have any further comments you wish to make, you're free to do so.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I do. I did check that as agreed with you. The exact surface is indeed 4.51 million, which is obtained in such a way that the pie slice --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat the figure of the surface area, because it was too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. The latter figure, 5454153.9. This is the entire circular piece. However, from that piece, another piece should be extracted which was under the BH Army control which is 872.664, so that in fact you did provide the exact figure in your first calculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much. Now, I just would like to note a transcript correction of the same page, 38584. The angle of the pie slice is 25 degrees, not 125 degrees as appears in yesterday's transcript. I'd now like to play a video which is P1450. In your report on this incident, which is the Markale II incident, you say at paragraph 79, which is on page 84 of the English version, that based -- you say: "The evacuation of the casualties was filmed from the very beginning by BH TV. Based on video recordings broadcast on the news bulletin on BH TV, we can conclude that BH TV cameramen filmed the evacuation from start to end." Is it your position that the TV camera crew was part of the conspiracy in this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That definitely is not my position. I only noted down my observation that the filming started practically before the incident itself, that the TV crew was present at the incident scene at Vasa Miskina and that it filmed its movement from that point to the incident site which can be seen. I'm not maintaining that the TV crew was part of any conspiracy but that it was present there and that it filmed what it did and what can be seen from the footage. So that's an observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We'll now play P1450, and we'll stop a few times during the video and discuss aspects of it which are discussed in your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, we have stopped -- we've stopped at 45.7 seconds. In the middle of the screen we see a man who appears to have had both legs cut off at approximately above the knee. In your report, at page 128 in B/C/S and page 84 in English, you say: "The unusual thing about this man is not only how he could have survived the explosion of a mortar shell without protection but also how such a strong explosion did not turn him parallel to the street." That's the end of that quote. Now, can we agree at least that both his legs have been cut off and that he is still alive at this point?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. That's what the report says.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, are you suggesting in your report, or today, that he was placed there after the detonation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For heaven's sake, how could I be able to -- how would I be able to claim something like that? Had I claimed anything like that, then I would have put it in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, then could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what exactly you meant when you said in your report: "The unusual thing about this man is not only how he could have survived the explosion of a mortar shell without protection but also how such a strong explosion did not turn him parallel to the street." What exactly are you getting at?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I want to say. When the explosion occurred or when an explosion of such a projectile occurs as is the 120-millimetre mortar shell, then the blast wave or the shockwave at this short distance is of great strength, and it is only natural that the person should be turned along the length of the street and thus not this way. What we spotted as a fact was that he was positioned in a different manner. If you look at the scene that we have now, you can see people lying down with their heads down the street, so along the length of the street, and that's consistent with a shockwave. It is only unusual, although possible, that people should survive such a shockwave, but it is highly unusual that they should survive such a shockwave without having been behind some sort of cover, without having been shielded from it in any way. So this is an observation that was made in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was observed that the position their bodies were in was not consistent with the propagation of the shockwave. Right in front of the people carrying someone you have, indeed, people who are positioned in accordance with the propagation of the shockwave. What that can suggest is another thing. I mean, what I have done is I have made an observation without any ulterior motives. Please read my text without any insinuations and without any subtext. Since you did read this carefully, I can tell, you could find that there are observations there which simply had to be made because they are of an unusual nature. As a scientist and a professional, I find it a duty to note that down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, do you accept that after this man was struck by the tremendous force of the shrapnel which took both of his legs off from approximately the knee down that he could have been turned in the air and, quite frankly, neither you nor I know exactly what the trajectory of his body was after he was struck by that enormous force?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I will agree with you. However, what the most probable trajectory was was the one indicated there, and consequently, his body should have been oriented in such a way as to lie in parallel to the length of the street. Well, he may have landed on the ground in such a way because of an obstacle that was in his way, but definitely not because the shockwave would have turned him this way, would have knocked him down this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We can play on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Stop. We've stopped at 1 minute, 20.3.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you, in the past few seconds we've seen what appear to be bodies strewn along this street. Do you accept that these are, in fact, bodies of persons who were killed in the detonation at this place and on this day?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see why I wouldn't accept it. I never claimed that they were brought to that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well. If we can play on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, we've stopped now at 1 minute and 26.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We see here a body of a person which is hanging over a rail. This is discussed in your report at page 129 in B/C/S, page 85 in English. You discussed this at length. Among other things, you say: "The wound is of such a nature that it is difficult to explain that it was caused by the explosion of a 120-millimetre mortar shell." Now, is it your position that the sabotage team which orchestrated this incident placed this body in civilian clothing at this location after the detonation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my position that there are indications... first and foremost, I stand firmly by the position that this is not an injury inflicted by the mortar shell shrapnel, nor could it ever be, no matter at what distance. That’s one. Two. This body is far from the centre of explosion, in a position which would be very hard to explain as to how it came about. Thirdly, there is a very small amount of blood around the body, and I had a photograph, a still which was very clear. So this body -- or, rather, the injuries there were not the result of a mortar shell, and as we can see, this is the centre of the explosion. We can see it in the background of the still. Nor is the blood around the individual consistent with the injury that we can observe on his body, nor does the photo documentation that we were able to review indicate that this individual is listed among the injured. So I don't know what sort of conclusion you could draw save for the fact that this body did not end up there as a result of the explosion of the -- a mortar shell for the above-stated reasons at the explosion site. It could not have been the result of that explosion, seeing the sort of injury it has and the position that the body is in. This is simply an observation. Let's be clear. I come from a different profession. And as for the injuries that can be inflicted by the sort of weaponry that I have been dealing with for the past 35 years, that is something I can talk about. Perhaps I cannot speak about certain medical aspects of this injury. However, as for the aspects that concern my profession, I absolutely stand by what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Mrs. Subotic, we can see from this screen shot a radius of 1 metre around this body, and I do not see an impact point within 1 metre of this body. What is it that makes you claim that the body is about a metre from the centre of the explosion?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say it was away 1 metre from the centre of the explosion. I rather said that the centre of the explosion is in the depth of the still, behind, further away from the post that we can see there, further down into the depth of the still.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The transcript of your evidence reads: "The body about a metre from the centre of explosion." Now, I'd like to press you on your assertion that this injury is inconsistent with the detonation of a 120-millimetre projectile. Do you accept, first of all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a moment. Could you give the transcript page reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. It's page 6 in today's transcript, at the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 6 and line?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Line 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we confirm with the witness. The transcript reads like this: "Secondly, the body is about a metre from the centre of explosion, and it is very hard to explain how this injury came about." Do you confirm having said so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say that it was 1 metre -- the body was 1 metre away from the centre of explosion. I said that it was hard to establish how the body came to be in the position that it was relative to the impact site, and that such a type of injury could not possibly have been produced by a mortar shell, because when a mortar shell is activated, the spray is dissipated rather than concentrated in its effect. And I said that it was not possible for there to be such a small amount of blood around the body given that the injury is so devastatingly great.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. I'll ask the CLSS to check the recording of today and to confirm whether doctor had really said that body was about a metre from the centre of explosion. We'll check it out. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I would like to put to you that you are not in a position to dismiss any of the number of the reasons why this body ended up in this place at this time, one of which is that he may well have been terribly injured and staggered to this location where he died. Another is that he died primarily through blast injury rather than shrapnel injury. Do you accept that there are other explanations for why this body was at this place, and those explanations are consistent with him having been killed by a 120-millimetre mortar detonation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned a moment ago, and I have to mention it again, the aspect of for how long a person may live after sustaining such an injury is not something I can testify to. I am not a medical doctor. For how long a person may live after sustaining such an injury is not something I can speak about or want to talk about. Now, the injury as seen here is indicative to me of an injury caused by a rifle-launched grenade or a solid object. Let's not speculate which sort of object that would be. At any rate, the fact that such a part of body is missing on the lateral side without an arm or the head missing is highly implausible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I must press you on your explanation which does not appear in your report that this injury might have been caused by a rifle-launched grenade. Could you explain clearly to the Trial Chamber your theory about how this body in civilian clothing with these injuries ended up at this location if he was not killed in the Markale II detonation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot explain something that I do not have evidence or parameters for. I only said that the body is indicative of injuries or the body has sustained injuries that were not sustained by a 120-millimetre mortar shell, and had they -- the injury been sustained at this spot, then there would have to have been a great deal more blood than there is, indeed, and that's what you have in the report. So the images that we see on our screen, there is a shadow, in fact, and the red-colour area that would be indicative of blood is practically minimal. What else can I add without going beyond the bounds of my profession?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If we could play on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Stop, please. We've stopped at 2:25.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, this body is -- appears at page 129 of your report, and that's at page 85 in English. Now, I just want to read a little part of what you said about this body. You said: "This man's bag has many shrapnel holes, although it was concealed by his body. Seventeen holes have been counted in the bag. If we take into account the undisputable fact that some shrapnel could have had enough energy to penetrate both the man's body and the bag, the number of holes is still too large. It is especially inexplicable why the holes have the same dimensions and a circular shape." So, first of all, can you give the Trial Chamber an estimate based on your expert knowledge of the number of pieces of shrapnel which result from the detonation of a 120-millimetre mortar projectile?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's certainly a very large number, and your conclusion does not affect what we wrote here. The order of magnitude is in the thousands. This is based on our experiments and it's a theoretical number. In practice it is never exactly the same. The density per square metre diminishes logarithmically in proportion with the distance from the centre of the explosion. It diminishes very fast. Yesterday, you said yourself that the lethal effect of this shell is until a distance of 17 metres, and it was also -- and at that distance there is one impact per square metre, one particle impact per square metre. What must be borne in mind is a circular shape, and we think this is a very unusual thing. If you take a better look at this bag, you will see that it is indeed circular, and this is basically impossible to achieve in an explosion of mines and shells. This is especially corroborated by the fact that in the photographic documentation there was at least one dead body on the stretchers of which pellets were found, and this was observed by forensic doctors, and I would like to point that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Have you personally ever examined a human body which had been killed following the detonation of a 120-millimetre mortar projectile?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I personally, together with forensic doctors, examined many bodies that were killed with -- from shotguns and hand-held firearms, but I've never been in a war, and I never had the opportunity to perform such an examination. And, by the way, that's for forensic doctors to do and not for me. I'm only present sometimes on such occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you clarify for the Trial Chamber why you are so certain that the man's bag was concealed by his body at the moment of detonation?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the body on the -- the position of the body on that street, and I think it is a dead body, my answer would be affirmative. He is holding something in his hand. There is no handle that goes over the shoulder so as to be on his back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So you are able to tell on the basis of this video alone the direction in which the man was travelling and whether his body was concealing his bag or was not concealing his bag at the moment of detonation? Is that your expert evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only on the basis of this video but also on the basis of the position of the body and the laws governing the propagation of shockwaves. It wouldn't -- for it not to result like this, he would have had to carry it over his shoulder, but that adds to the oddity, but does not allow for conclusive statements. However, the fact that there are shrapnel holes of a circular shape is something inexplicable because it's impossible to achieve.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, Mrs. -- Mrs. Subotic, you've been alluding to that a couple of times. I want you to come straight out about what your theory is here. Is it your theory that this man was killed with some kind of small-bore weapon at a different location and then he was transported to Markale Market and he was scattered among -- or placed, rather, among the bodies of people who had been killed in that explosion? Please explain your theory clearly to the Trial Chamber as to how this body ended up in this location at this time.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is not a word saying that this body was brought there, so I can discard that immediately. I don't know how you came up with the thesis that it was brought there. What was observed here is the following: There is a dead body at the site that suffered injuries from a large number of small projectiles of a circular shape and they cannot be found in the centre of the explosion. This does not exclude the possibility that something else exploded there that contained pellets such as a hand grenade. Anything that contains pellets, that may also have exploded there. There is a fact here, namely that the body that is there, and I'm not talking about bringing bodies there or taking them away, this body is in an unusual position, technically speaking, and it suffered injuries from small projectiles of a circular shape, and we can see that on that person's clothing and back. And I repeat, a 120-millimetre mortar shell does not contain any pellets. So this man could have come to harm right there, but how we cannot say because there is no material evidence, or there are no investigation results contributing to the -- to a -- to a clarification, but the fact is that the body is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I just want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 12, line 19, it says: "[In English] They cannot be found in the centre of the explosion." [Interpretation] The witness did not say "in the centre of explosion" but "in such an explosion." I don't think she mentioned the centre of the explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I note, Mrs. Subotic, in your report there's not one mention of a simultaneous detonation of a hand grenade. That's an explanation which you've come up with today for the first time. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not venture into speculation, and that's why there's no mention of it. You asked me whether it was brought there, and I only spoke about possibilities, because pellets are contained in the assets mentioned. I did not speculate. I analysed traces. I drew conclusion based on hard evidence, and what I found is listed as a fact rather than a speculation of mine about what might have happened if something else happened and so on. I cannot deal with that. It's a fact, however, that this body was found where it was found and in the state in which it was found.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can we play on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We've obviously skipped forth in time to a time where some of the first UNPROFOR troops attended the scene. We've stopped now at 3 minutes and 48.6 seconds. My question to you is this: In your report you have set forth only two possibilities for the Markale II incident. One is that it was a static detonation by a device placed presumably in the middle of this busy street, the second that it was a roof-top delivery. Have you seen in any of the reports by those who physically inspected the site, such as these two men here, or in the reports prepared by the BiH MUP persons who physically inspected the site to suggest that they thought that this was either a static detonation in the middle of the street or a roof-top delivery?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I just received -- just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While the interpreters will listen to the audio recording again, but I just received an informal report from the court reporter that Mrs. Subotic actually said as was noted in the transcript. I'm referring to the part where she said: "Secondly, the body is about a metre from the centre of explosion, and it is very hard to explain how this injury came about." This is how it was -- she listened to the section, and that was how it was interpreted into English. Yes. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning, Excellencies. Good morning to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will start with the most recent things. Today, on page 11, you were asked whether you had ever examined a victim of a 120-millimetre mortar shell. Since you were a court expert, are you familiar with the characteristics of wounds inflicted by various assets?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, because together with my colleagues, forensic doctors, I must draw conclusions, and there are books dealing with the details of this matter. What I want to say here is that any statement of mine about the possibility of wounding, firstly and foremostly refers to lethal assets, and from that point of view such a wound is impossible. I mean, it's impossible that such a wound should have been inflicted by a 120-millimetre mortar shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Today you mentioned you didn't want to speculate without an investigation and a thorough study. Since you are a court expert, have you ever heard of cases where the dead are evacuated before the living? Is that usual?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen an evacuation of the dead before an evacuation of the living.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you expect -- expecting a priority to be given to the wounded, an on-site investigation with measurements, photographs being taken, and so on?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is usual for an on-site investigation to be conducted before changing anything at the site. That is standard procedure, what can be found in any textbook, but of course that doesn't mean that the wounded should not be removed. I took part in many investigations where the dead were still at the site when we arrived, and that is considered normal procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It was not recorded that I said in my question "before moving the dead," meaning that the living should certainly be removed. Is all we see in the footage of these two incidents such as the manner of evacuation, the handling of the wounded and dead bodies, the dragging of the bodies and so forth? Does that tally with your experience?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I must say that I have no experience with such massive incidents. I only know with instances of a smaller number of people being harmed, but after removing the -- after removing the wounded --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- everything should have remained unchanged for an on-site investigation to be conducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So it is your testimony that the bodies should have remained there until there was some kind of on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be customary procedure. According to the customary procedure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Customary -- custom in where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any crime investigation procedure including an on-site investigation. It is the same everywhere. It's not a local procedure. This is how on-site investigations are conducted according to textbooks. It would be a customary procedure for ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Defence is very grateful to you for having presented several possibilities as to how things happened. However, we are even more grateful to you for having presented your analysis based on hard evidence as to how things didn't happen. The Prosecution obviously did not --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry. Is this a question? What -- what's going here? This is -- this looks like total commentary to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you wrapping up your re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Excellencies. I'm moving to a different topic, but with all due respect, Madam Gustafson's questions were two or three pages long. I'm just trying to do a little introductory of perhaps two or three sentences into my next topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's an inappropriate comment. Just ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Please, did the Defence ever ask you to establish how things happened or how things did not happen or what was unusual with regard to those cases?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. The Defence did not ask me either to establish how things were or how things were not. As a court expert and based on my long years of experience, when I am faced with an incident or five or ten incidents, however many happened here, my task is to analyse all the material available to me, and based on all the material and hard evidence, my task is to try and establish first and foremost how things happened and if -- of course if that is possible, to spot all the inconsistencies and omissions, and based on that, my task is to come up with the most likely outcome, i.e., how things evolved. As a result of that, we can also conclude how things didn't happen, but this is just a byproduct, which is necessary because in this case we found quite a large number of inconsistencies that happened during the investigations. I'm not going to go into the reasons why these inconsistencies happened. I'm not judging the professionalism, the custody of the material or any such thing. What I had in my hands was hard evidence based on the investigations carried out by other people and based on my own investigation that I carried out on the spot. The objective was to establish, if at all possible, and if that was not possible, it was our task to establish why that was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Here we were shown a stabiliser and several photos. Do you remember if you carried out the physical inspection of that object that you were given yesterday during your previous testimonies and -- or during your previous stays here, and was somebody from the Defence present when you did that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at the end of 2010, courtesy of the Prosecution, I had an occasion to inspect the stabiliser. Mr. Marko Sladojevic was present while I was doing that. We also took photos on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you observe the mobility of the ignition cap as we witnessed yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First this is not an ignition cap. It is the standard charge. We did not notice that. We even checked that, and yesterday I testified -- testified to that effect in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That primary charge or the casing of the primary charge, could it dry out in any way? Could it be become loose over the time between the first inspection and what you were able to observe yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before you answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's clearly a leading question of the highest order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, the first part in particular was very leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: My question is this: How could something like that happen? Could it become looser spontaneously?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I have to say -- or describe precisely how things are done. I suppose that in this courtroom there is a hunter, at least one hunter. The standard charge is very similar to the bullet for a hunting rifle, or a jacket for the hunting rifle bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please slow down for the sake of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how far we got. It looks like a -- the jacket of a hunting rifle to a large extent. There is a jacket, and on that jacket there are imprints that we saw yesterday. The ignition cap is in there. This is the central metal part that we observed yesterday. And there are two openings or holes for the tools with which the bullet is mounted in the stabiliser. It is fixed by way of a coil or with the help of a coil which, as you know, locks itself. However, from the moment it is fixed, something has to be added like cement or shellac or something similar. Once that is dry, it serves as the additional security from uncoiling or unscrewing. It's a safety mechanism. The conclusion is that that jacket over the period of time could not have become unscrewed without the use of force. So it could not become as mobile as we could see that it had become yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Sladojevic show interest, and did he ask questions about the mobility and the nature of that ignition cap during the first inspection?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that inspection I believe that there was a representative of the Prosecution present, but I don't remember who it was. Perhaps it was even Mr. Gaynor, but I'm not sure. We discussed that matter, because we noticed in the documents that we perused before that, and I told Mr. Sladojevic that it was a very firm bond, and he even checked my words on the spot.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D7454 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at the two photos in the top row and can you describe the position of the little holes. Can you also tell us whether in your view the distance between the fins in the top row is the same or is it perhaps much bigger on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance between the fins where? I did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The arch between the fins --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry. If Dr. Karadzic is going to repeat this question, then I ask that he do it in a non-leading way and not the leading way he did it the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll come back to this later. I'm interested in the arch, whether it is identical or not. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber, based on the comparison between the photos of the stabiliser that was taken on the 5th of March, 2010, where do the opening for the key meet, and what is their position in the two different objects? Are they identical? If they're not, why are they not identical?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it's not identical. You can see it in the photos. Courtesy of Mr. Gaynor yesterday, I saw something that I could not find in the documentation, because the photos were not clear. Yesterday, I dictated that for the record. I'm very glad that I had an occasion to see that. What we see here are two projectiles which were not fired from the same asset, and it's quite visible in both photos, the top photos and the bottom photos. The difference exists, but as much -- as far as I can see in the top row that is marked and in the lower photos, the ignition cap has been altered, I claim with full responsibility. This is a hole, and this is the jacket of the primer which can be seen based on the lines that have been drawn, L1 and L2, the place where the pin hit the primer, and we saw a mark yesterday. It's a piece of forensic evidence that cannot be refuted by any claims. This is hard evidence in forensic terms. This is the imprint of the pin of the primer, and you can see that it is completely different. It is in different places. It is very discernible in the photos, and I claim with full responsibility that these two projectiles were not fired from the same mortar.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can either the top right or the bottom right photo be zoomed in, because I would like the witness to mark something for us. It's a much better view if you zoom in on the lower right image. So zoom it in as much as you can, the bottom right image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we move the -- yes. Would you like to zoom in further?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please use the pen and mark what you have just explained for us. What exists here? What doesn't exist there? The position of the holes and alterations on the primer or the detonating cap.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1 denotes the position of the holes, and as for the primer or the detonating cap and the imprint on it is marked by number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sign and put today's date, because we have to have photos admitted one by one, and in a minute I'm going to ask you to mark the other one. Today we're the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So before we admit this, Mr. Karadzic, is it your case that what we saw yesterday, the actual stabiliser, is not the identical one which we see in the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we see that in this photo. However, the other one, the one that was found in the photo file, is not the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't follow. So it is your case there exists two stabilisers. So what we have at the moment, actual material, had come from different source. Is it your case, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the position of the Defence that this stabiliser is being ascribed to the shell which exploded at Markale II, but it is not the same stabiliser. Either there was some sort of manipulation done in the photo file or the Chamber was given a different stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can Mr. Karadzic repeat what he said last.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat what you said last.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there are two stabilisers, two different stabilisers, whereas there should only be one. It was either the case that the photo file which was produced right over there, there was a stabiliser planted, or the Chamber was sent a different stabiliser. It is not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. If I could just add something for the record since you've asked about our case, and I think it's probably more accurate for us to say that it's our case that it can't be established beyond a reasonable doubt which side fired the mortar that landed in Markale on the 28th of August, 1995. As part of the testimony of this witness, we are asserting certain things about the stabiliser that is her conclusions, and we're attempting to show why those conclusions would be reasonable, but it's not -- our case is not dependent on the existence of one or two different stabilisers. I thought I just should make that clear so that in your judgement we don't have any confusion. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was just trying to understand the point of the question. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3553, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In order not to be confused, there exists two stabilisers in your custody? Yes, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No -- well, yes -- I mean, there's a Markale I stabilisers and there's a Markale II stabiliser. What we're looking at right now is the Markale II stabiliser. I understand that the Defence's position on this, to be a little more specific, is that both of the stabilisers look as though they've been run over by a vehicle. Both of the stabilisers bear the markings MKM74 KB9307, both of the stabilisers are almost identical in appearance apart from the positioning of the holes at the top of that -- that part of the stabiliser which Your Honours were rotating with your own fingers yesterday. So I understand that that is the Defence position. Why exactly one would want to produce two stabilisers, I have no idea, and that is entirely unclear in the Defence's submission so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is the amount of time for which you should pause between the question and answer. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have the left-hand side, and on the right-hand side can we at least keep the circle. Good. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us now which features on the right-hand side of the screen are not matched by that on the left, do not exist?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the standard charge jacket on both the left and the right-hand side, across that particular jacket we have a line drawn which on the left-hand side was marked with L1. It is a reference line enabling us to observe the trace that was, in forensic terms, different with these two stabilisers. What we can see clearly is that the imprint of the primer which touches the bottom parts -- the bottom indentations that are there for the tools to screw or unscrew, and as for the jacket of the standard charge which we can see in the photo file, that particular imprint of the standard charge jacket is positioned differently on the stabiliser that was shown to us in the courtroom yesterday. So there's a difference between that one in the photo file and the one shown in the courtroom. And this is forensic evidence to the fact that the two projectiles were fired from two different mortars, because the imprint that the firing pin makes is something that is typical of the mortar and not the projectile. If you want me to, I can mark it on this image.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please do so. It may be more helpful to have both images side by side. And can you also tell us how you would estimate the degree of the arches between the fins left and right. If we look at 360 degrees, what would the arch be on the one on the left and on the one on the right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can tell that it's not the same. I don't think it's necessary to mark the arch at all. We saw yesterday that depending on how we rotate, the position will be different. This isn't necessary. The key and basic reference information is the line that goes across the standard charge jacket which is solid, because it will rotate always as one part, whereas if we rotate the outer ring, then the position of the line will be different. Since it's already been moved from its initial position, and that it has been moved from its position is something that we were able to glean yesterday, had it not been moved, then it would make sense to discuss this. As things stand, I don't see what the point of it would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you use the electronic pen and mark on the primer itself the differences between the two images and especially the line that is indented in the primer on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I have the assistance of the usher, please. [In English] Thank you. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us the distance between the imprint that the pin made from L1 line and the distance between the imprint and the L2 line?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that the point is that the imprint is positioned differently. As for the centre, perhaps we should put it in AutoCAD and then measure the distances. As it is now, I would simply be guessing. If you want an accurate answer to the question, we could transpose the image into AutoCAD and make exact measurements. This wouldn't be difficult at all. Although the difference is quite obvious, even to those who are not members of the profession. And I can tell you again that no expert can be found who would disagree with me, because this is the elementary basic parameter against which one would assess the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you make the marking, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, given that the witness has clarified her evidence on this point, I wonder if we are not wasting an enormous amount of time. She said that it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber has discussed it. It is for the Defence how to proceed, so we left it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: But, Mr. Gaynor, I have to say I understand why you made the intervention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3554, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for the record, I'd like to make a --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- comment. Shall we zoom out from this photo. See the original 1D7454 in its entirety. It is Defence that noted the ERN number at the bottom of the document. I think it should read -- the last two digits of ERN number should read 29 instead of 27. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellencies. I tender all the four photographs, the bottom two indicate the distance between the imprint and lines 1 and 2. That's 1D7454.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3555, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's finish the issue of Markale. I have to say again that the Defence is interested in proving that it didn't happen, and of course it is up to the Prosecution to prove how and that it was. Were you the first ones to take the view about the activation of the device at Markale I site?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That particular view was something that I certainly came across in the documents that I was made available by the Tribunal. There were various documents taking up that view, so, no, I was not the first one to take up that position or to advocate it, no. I merely took that view on the basis of physical evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have P1441. Thank you. Can we now have the last page. I apologise. Page 26 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will now read for you what the team, and I think it's the French team, concluded. Item 2: [As read] "[In English] The crater itself and the damage of the stall around the crater, the trajectory of the splinter was upwards, indicated that the explosion happened at ground level." [Interpretation] How does this fit with your position?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I received in interpretation was that everything indicated that the explosion occurred at ground level; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, based on the traces and the damage to the stalls.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that would fit with our conclusions, and we did say that the explosion -- and there is damage to that effect which was filmed, that there is damage to the bottom side of the stalls. This is consistent with my conclusions, and I think that I did comment as much in relation to that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Pages 19, 16, 23, 25 of the same document contain quite a few elements indicative of tampering with the crater by different people and with various tools.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karadzic, that's a totally inappropriate comment. Would you like to add anything, Ms. Gustafson?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: No, that was it, Your Honours, or if it is the preface to a question, then it's a leading one. If he wants to show her particular aspects of the document and have her comment on them, then he should just do that without this leading commentary.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. While the objection is well founded, before we take our break I would like to ask that you direct the Prosecution to select one of them to make objections to the testimony. We did allow both of them to participate in the direct examination, and we didn't have any problem with that, but I think it's only proper that one person be designated to make the objections to Dr. Karadzic's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see the time. It's time to take a break. Just for planning purpose, how long would you expect your re-examination to last?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not long. Less than one session. A lot less than one session. What I cited, the pages that I cited, was for the participants, for their reference, to find the information I wished to refer them to. It wasn't for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You didn't refer to only the page numbers. You said something else about the content. We'll take a break for half an hour and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, I made some submissions earlier about the Markale I stabiliser and the Markale II stabiliser. They weren't as clear as they could have been. I'd like to clarify the position for the transcript. The Markale I stabiliser is P1967. The Markale II stabiliser is P1454. Both are available for inspection by Your Honours. Both are in the custody of the Registrar, not the Prosecution. The discussion this morning concerned a comparison of the Markale II stabiliser which Your Honours personally inspected yesterday, which is P1454, compared with the contemporaneous photo file of the Markale II stabiliser. I hope that's a little clearer than my earlier explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And I received an interim report from the CLSS that there was indeed an interpretation error. What was recorded as: "Secondly, the body is about a metre from the centre of explosion" should have read, "Two, this body is far from the centre of explosion, in a position which would be very hard to explain as to how it came about." I expect that the CLSS would file an official record about this. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before I break I asked you whether you were the first and the only one who mentioned the possibility that an explosion had occurred at Markale I.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please let us see 1D26766.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please take a look at what is written here. The date is the 9th of February. It says -- it mentions Fahrudin Orucevic. Do you know that name?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Orucevic, as far as I know, worked for that institute over there, and I also think that at a certain point he worked for Pretis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. What is this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The thesis here is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, in order to tender some document, you need to put some foundational question to the witness so that the Chamber is satisfied as to its provenance, et cetera. This is a news clipping in "Tanjug"? Yes. You should put the question --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I asked a question before the break whether Mrs. Subotic was the first or the only one who put forward such a thesis, and she answered in the negative, that there had been such indications of others holding the same position. I'm showing this document which was produced four days after the document, and Fahrudin Orucevic is trying to avoid Sky News because he felt uneasy due to his presence at the site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor or Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll deal with this one. First of all, this is, of course, emanating from "Tanjug," the Belgrade-based news agency of the Belgrade authorities. Second, this is a matter which could have been raised in the direct examination of this witness and does not appear to arise directly out of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor's first point goes to weight. The second point is that he called into question during his cross-examination her theory about the market-place -- the detonation being by remote control, so it's perfectly proper for Dr. Karadzic to show -- try to introduce some evidence which corroborates her testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D3556, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the first day, on page 70, you answered that the direction was established based on a drawing of the shrapnel -- the position of the shrapnel. Was -- were directions thus established in criminal cases. You probably know what I'm talking about. You spoke about the trajectory of the shell based on the dispersion pattern on the ground. Apart from establishing the source of fire, was -- is that method also used in criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about the accuracy of the method and its use and the reasons for introducing such a method. Its primary purpose is what you mentioned, namely, to establish the trajectory in order to be able to respond. As for criminal proceedings, I have not yet seen it being applied. It's a -- it's the best method that was available, although it is not perfect.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Figure 52 from the G5 incident. That is the shelling report. D3542. In Serbian it's page 93. Can we please zoom in. Even more. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you draw the left limit of the arch around this dispersion pattern using your electronic pen, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Is this what you wanted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please sign and date this.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D3557, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at image 46 on page 88 in the Serbian version. And please tell us under what conditions can such a dispersion pattern occur in the centre of the street if the trajectory is as marked here?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat her answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said this dispersion pattern will be completely differently oriented, and it would be shaped as in image 48, marked red.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Subotic heard the question, but the English interpretation was not complete. If a shell had flown in as alleged in the indictment, what would be the left arch be like? Can you tell us about this fence? If things had happened as alleged in the indictment, that is, if the shell had flown in as alleged there, what kind of angle would have been required for it to miss the fence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mrs. Subotic, could you repeat your answer. Please put a pause before answering the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. First of all, the descent angle should have been large, because the impact was very near the fence. On the other hand, the fence would certainly be much more heavily damaged. I don't know if we would see it, but this fence would have been more badly damaged, because it would show traces in the rear and the centre part, bearing in mind that the explosion occurred at a height of 65 centimetres. Maybe the shockwave would also cause some deformation. It's hard to say because we're talking about the gate that is a movable part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I'd just like to put it on the record that the question was framed in the hypothetical in terms of what would have happened if the shell had flown in as alleged in the indictment. However, in the answer, the witness stated that the height of the explosion was 65 centimetres, and I just want to point out that that is the height based on her theory of what happened. There is no specific height indicated in the contemporaneous investigation documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, in the investigation of such explosions, is there a hierarchy of evidence? What is most valuable in determining the impact of a mortar shell? Which are the most important elements? The crater, the dispersion pattern? What is the most important thing?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most important evidence is the pattern on the ground at the site of impact. That means the traces of shrapnel. Secondly, any other trace caused by the explosion, also the position of the stabiliser, but we depart from what is left over at the site, and in this case it's, firstly, the pattern on the asphalt and the traces of the shockwave on the vehicle next to the fence. I must say, however, that in this case everything matches. Even the stabiliser is found in such a position as to match the trajectory and the descent angle. Here the position of the stabiliser matches all other physical evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 67. The same document as before. Who took this photograph, and what does it represent?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Photographs 1 and 2 were taken by us when we went to see the site, and I believe it was in September 2010.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure about the year.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the same crater --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry. There's a lot of overlap. I think we're missing a lot of information in the transcript as a result.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: When were these photos taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These photos were taken on the 11th of September, 2010, when we visited the site as instructed by the Defence and the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: From there please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please tell us what these images represent.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This image shows two craters, crater one where the first shell landed, and crater two where another landed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which azimuth was determined, and are they the same or similar?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not understand your question. When you say "identical," identical to what? You mean identical to what the investigators had established?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I had in mind the two photos, the two craters. Did you determine the azimuth? What was it? Does it point to the same launching place?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, these are two craters, and when the CSB investigated them they said that they found only one crater. That would be my first remark as regards the facts. And the second remark is as follows: It says further on in the text that these azimuths -- or, rather, that one of them is not identical. The azimuth that was determined by the investigator is not the same, and we already discussed that during the cross-examination. The investigators erroneously established the azimuth, and you can see that also in the figure --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not understand the last bit of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which of these two craters were investigated by the investigators?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. No, no, no. It's impossible. Mrs. Subotic, please speak very slowly. The interpreters were not able to catch up with your speed. And could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you start over from the second point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know where the interpreters caught up with me. In any case, the investigators who did their work in 1995 investigated just one crater because they did not locate the second one. They simply couldn't find it. And they determined an erroneous azimuth for the crater that they investigated. In the courtroom, we showed that a couple of days ago, and it can only be seen in photo number 37. That azimuth, as determined by the investigators, is erroneous, because the compass was placed in a wrong place and on a wrong slant, and we double-checked all that based on the traces that we found on the spot, and we established that there is a difference of some 33 degrees in what they established and what we could establish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at figure 55. Is this where the shell landed in Klare Cetkin 22 on the 22nd of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could you start over again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This is the impact point in Klare Cetkin Street near number 4, and the photo was taken on the 18th of September, 2010. The incident happened on the 22nd of January as was stated in the question that was put to me. The photo was taken on the 22nd of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please mark the part of the curb that was not later covered with concrete. Can you see that? The part of the curb that was damaged in the incident that was not covered with concrete subsequently.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how does that tally with the claims on the size of the crater and the shell calibre?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see based on the red markings on the metre or the tape-measure, you can see that the crater was about 60 centimetres or even more than that, more than that, actually, and that that would correspond to a 122-millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Date and initial.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 120-millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Admission, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D3558, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Figure 63, please. Could you please tell us what was the trajectory that was determined by the CSB as opposed to the trajectory that was determined by Captain Verdy?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We marked the two. The blue marking denote the trajectory that was determined by the CSB Sarajevo, whereas Captain Verdy determined the trajectory that was marked in red. And in the case of Klare Cetkin incident, we checked the physical evidence, and as for the second shell, we checked that based on the video-clip, and we got a match, which was very good, and that's why we decided to use Captain Verdy's findings, because we considered them to be confirmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where do the trajectories meet in Captain Verdy's case?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They meet -- I believe that the trajectory was 3.270 from the place of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does the difference in determining the trajectory -- what -- could it happen by mistake? Could it be just an error?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid not, because all the physical evidence on the ground that we inspected and the photos from the photo file that was compiled by Barry Hogan clearly point to the fact that Captain Verdy was right. So I wouldn't agree that it was just by mistake, although mistakes do happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like to draw your attention to one part of your report dealing with modified air-bombs. You were asked on page 95, on the second day, by Mr. Gaynor about FAB-100 with retarding system. Is retarding used when a rocket is launched from the ground?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In ground delivery of a FAB-100 the retardation is not used because it would be pointless.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked about the ways the engines are checked. Are only new assets checked, or is every series of old assets also checked? What is checked before it starts being used by the troops?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before assets are used or become part of weaponry everything is checked. Every segment of such an asset is checked in great detail and very precisely. However, it seems to me that you asked me about every new series. During the manufacturing process, every series is checked and double-checked before it is used to complete lethal weapons. Every segment that is manufactured, every new series has to undergo a complete, military control at every level of production in order to be used to complete any other assets. So if you're talking about charges, every new series of charge is tested and then it is used to complete warheads. Also the same applies to warheads, to the explosive that is built into a warhead. So every series of every product is treated as a new product which needs to be tested before being used.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "As it was for the first time." In transcript, should be ended: "As it was for the first time."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is after the production. All controls of the series are made to see whether the products meet all the standards. If it is concluded that not all the standards are met, the product is returned for additional checks, and if it is established that the error is not going to have an impact on the function, it will still be received for use, but that has to be done by a commission depending on the use of the product that is being used to complete a certain asset.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was a common practice at Pretis with this regard?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what Pretis did in that regard. However, Pretis could not do anything differently than the JNA regulations, and the JNA regulations were what I just told you. So they could not act outside of the system that they operated within. Everything functioned in the same way. Everybody had to comply with the same rules. There was no single company that produced for the army that could apply their own practice that would fall out of the rules of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at 1D7452. There is no translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to read or perhaps I will read. We'll ask you to read, but do it slowly. 1D7452. The heading, date, and text.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska. Logistics sector. Technical department. Strictly confidential, No." And then 1. I can't read what -- /34/2-2- -- and this could be 685 or 665. Date, 20 July 1995. "To be delivered to the command of the 27th POB 1" or "I. HD Pretis," probably holding, "for their information." Under 1: "The command of the 27th POB will deliver to HD Pretis 50 pieces of rocket engines, K13 (out of the total of probably 200) which need to undergo checks and a technical examination." Under 2: "In the accompanying transport, the 27th PB -- POB," or, rather, probably, "in the transport on the way back, the 27th POB will hand over to the HD Pretis also an ME rocket (in parts)."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at who it was who sent out the letter. Thank you. Can it be marked -- admitted and marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How does this fit with your knowledge of the interaction between the logistics base and Pretis with regard to rocket engines?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, obviously engines are being sent over for testing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we will mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D3559, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D28719. There is many of them, but I'll just take this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that each series is tested. Can you please read out slowly the top part, because the bottom part is self-explanatory.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the heading says: "The Technical Testing Centre, Nikinci grounds, sent to Pretis. Subject --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just take it slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The subject is: "Testing of ammunition on testing grounds."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what ammunition is being sent? You don't have to read everything.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the ammunition of the 120-millimetre shell, which is a light contact fuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it a marked series?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. The sort of testing required is also designated on a number of performances including extreme temperatures and the points are indicated here or items which refer to the so-called PKP document. It's a document which reads: "The regulations governing the control and quality of product," and the items listed here are references to the same items contained in the PKP manual, indicating exactly the performances that are requested to be tested.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have a look at who the sender is. Can you read this out, please?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Director of Quality Control of the Pretis, Milo Jokic," a graduate of mechanical engineering.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the accused please repeat the date that he mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you note the interpreter's request?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I merely repeated the date, 3 January 1994. And can it be admitted and marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, I presume the accused is tendering this because it happens to contain the letters MKM74 in the middle of it. I'm perplexed as to why he hasn't questioned the witness about that. Those are the letters which appear on the Markale II projectile. But I have no objection to its admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where do we see that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Under the third indent under the words "sastav elemenata."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you read out that line, Mrs. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Standard gunpowder charge MKM74."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D3560, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, a response to Mr. Gaynor. I could not address this in the examination-in-chief because it was only during the cross-examination that the fact that the assets were being tested was challenged. It's the army that would ask for testing, and this is evidence of the fact that assets were being sent out for testing, every series.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think that was -- that was the point of Mr. Gaynor, but let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, at page 92, line 9, you were asked -- or, rather, you were given the assertion that the rockets were not designed for simultaneous but for consecutive launch. Can you tell us, when it comes to a multi-barrel rocket launcher with three or four rows, what is exactly being fired simultaneously and what is being fired consecutively?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't really fully understood the question, but at any rate, the rockets designed for a multi-barrel -- could the Chamber and those present in the courtroom bear in mind that when I say "rockets," I mean a military asset which has a rocket engine and a warhead -- and a warhead, and of course when I say a "rocket engine," I mean something else. So when we're talking about assets of rocket artillery such as multi-barrel rocket launchers which launch rockets from barrels, from tubes, the so-called land rocket artillery, projectiles are always fired in single shots or in bursts or in salvos, and it's the same rockets that will be fired. Of course, depending on the objective that one wants to achieve, rockets can be fired in different ways. I'm not sure that I have understood the question properly. At any rate, to the best of my understanding, always the same rockets are being fired.
